# ALYRA

> ALYRA is a private asset-backed lending business in Australia. It provides discreet, secured loans from $50,000 to $5 million against high-value collateral including luxury watches, jewellery and diamonds, fine art, classic and luxury cars, gold bullion, and designer handbags. Clients keep ownership of the asset, which is held in secure, insured custody for the loan term and returned once the loan is repaid. No public listing, no auction, no obligation.

Key facts:

- Legal entity: ALYRA GROUP PTY LTD (ABN 72 699 671 291)
- Licensed pawnbroker: licence 4817352 (Queensland)
- Second-hand dealer licence: 4817352 (Queensland)
- Loan range: $50,000 – $5,000,000 AUD
- Service area: Australia-wide enquiries — Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Gold Coast; private appointments by arrangement
- Contact: hello@alyra.com.au (by appointment only)
- Enquiries: https://www.alyra.com.au/valuation/ — confidential valuation request, specialist response typically within one business day

## Insights articles

- [What actually determines the value of a fine watch in 2026](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/what-determines-fine-watch-value/): How a fine watch's realisable value is assessed — brand, reference, condition, originality, documentation, provenance, market demand and sale channel
- [Which prestige car marques actually hold their value in Australia in 2026](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/which-prestige-car-marques-hold-value-australia/): Which marques retain value in Australia — Ferrari, Porsche, Lamborghini and others — and why model, specification, kilometres, documentation and sale channel decide the real number
- [Gold and bullion as collateral: a practical guide](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/gold-and-bullion-as-collateral/): How bullion is assessed as lending security — purity, weight, refiner, ownership, allocated vs unallocated storage, lender control, valuation basis, haircuts, liquidity and legal enforceability
- [How much can I borrow against a Rolex in Australia?](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-much-can-i-borrow-against-a-rolex-australia/): There is no fixed Rolex loan figure — how realisable market value, condition, documentation and ALYRA's $50,000–$5,000,000 lending range shape the amount, and when a collection is needed to reach the minimum
- [How watch service history affects your loan offer](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-watch-service-history-affects-your-loan-offer/): How service records are weighed in a loan assessment — when documented, authorised servicing strengthens an offer, when replaced original parts reduce vintage value, and what to do if records are incomplete
- [How lenders assess blue-chip art as collateral](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-lenders-assess-blue-chip-art-as-collateral/): How a blue-chip painting is assessed as loan collateral — identity, liquidity and control tests, provenance and title, catalogue raisonné status, market depth, condition, custody and why there is no universal loan-to-value percentage
- [How lenders assess independent and complicated watches](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-lenders-assess-independent-and-complicated-watches/): How independent and complicated watches are assessed as collateral — reference-level comparable sales, originality, complications and serviceability, condition, provenance, custody and CITES strap considerations for cross-border movement
- [How lenders assess Rolex, Patek Philippe and Richard Mille watches in Australia](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-lenders-assess-rolex-patek-philippe-richard-mille-watches-australia/): How the three most recognised luxury-watch names are assessed as loan collateral — identity and configuration, completed sales and buyer depth, condition and originality, Rolex CPO, Patek Philippe archive extracts, Richard Mille warranty records, serviceability, custody and the Australian PPSA, National Credit Code and pawnbroking framework
- [Reading an auction result before you rely on it](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/reading-an-auction-result-before-you-rely-on-it/): What an art auction result does and does not prove — hammer price vs price realised, bought-in and withdrawn lots, attribution and cataloguing, condition reports, guarantees and irrevocable bids, bidder depth, currency and CPI adjustment, Australian resale royalty and export controls, and net recoverable value
- [The case for liquidity without giving up ownership](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/liquidity-without-giving-up-ownership/): When borrowing against a valuable asset makes more sense than selling it — what retaining ownership does and does not mean under a security interest, comparing net cash rather than headline values, custody and loss of use, repayment and exit planning, sale timing risk, and Australian PPSA, pawnbroking, CGT and resale-royalty considerations
- [Lending against Argyle pink diamonds](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/lending-against-argyle-pink-diamonds/): How an Argyle pink diamond is assessed as loan security — verifying Argyle provenance via Diamond Check, laser inscriptions and Chain of Custody documents, independent grading of natural vs treated colour, colour grade, carat weight, clarity and cut, why the 2020 mine closure does not set an individual stone's value, PPSR searches, and ALYRA's secure custody until repayment
- [How much can I borrow against my Richard Mille watch in Australia?](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-much-can-i-borrow-against-richard-mille-watch-australia/): Why there is no fixed Richard Mille loan figure or universal loan-to-value percentage — ALYRA's $50,000–$5,000,000 luxury-watch range, net recoverable value versus retail and asking prices, reference-level differences between RM 67-02 and RM 027, 2026 Phillips results read as market evidence rather than borrowing benchmarks, warranty and service records, and Australian pawnbroking and National Credit Code treatment
- [How much can I borrow against my gold bullion in Australia?](https://www.alyra.com.au/insights/how-much-can-i-borrow-against-my-gold-bullion-australia/): Why spot price, collateral value and loan amount are three different numbers — verified weight, purity and refiner, dealer and mint buy prices versus retail, haircuts and loan-to-value as separate steps, ALYRA's $50,000–$5,000,000 bullion range, LBMA Good Delivery versus private 1kg bars, 2026 gold volatility, and Queensland redemption periods
